articles.title: बौद्धनाथमा अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिमा राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप, कसले रोक्यो सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको नियुक्ति पत्र ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति तीन महिनादेखि अध्यक्षविहीन छ । संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालय मातहतको यो महत्वपूर्ण निकायमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको सिफारिस भइसके पनि राजनीतिक स्वार्थका कारण नियुक्तिले अझै पूर्णता पाउन सकेको छैन । अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको निर्णय भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिँदा सरकारको नियतमाथि नै प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ ।

गत असार १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयअनुसार संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालयले बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिको अध्यक्षमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामालाई नियुक्त गर्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो । तर विडम्बना, निर्णय भएको यति समय बितिसक्दा पनि लामाले नियुक्तिपत्र पाएका छैनन् ।

समितिका अध्यक्षसहित पाँच पदाधिकारी नियुक्त गरिए पनि अध्यक्ष लामाबाहेक सबै सदस्यले नियुक्तिपत्र बुझिसकेका छन् । अध्यक्षलाई मात्रै रोक्नुको कारण काठमाडौं–३ का रास्वपा सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे रहेको आरोप छ ।

स्थानीयका अनुसार सांसद पाण्डेले आफ्ना निकट व्यक्तिलाई अध्यक्ष बनाउन दबाब दिएपछि लामाको नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिएको हो । लामो समयदेखि समिति नेतृत्वविहीन हुँदा गुठियारदेखि स्थानीय सरोकारवालासम्म सरकारसँग जवाफ माग्न थालेका छन् । उनीहरूको चेतावनी छ, ‘रास्वपाभित्रको जुंगाको लडाइँको छायाँ बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिमा पार्न मिल्दैन ।’

दुई कार्यकाल सफलतापूर्वक अध्यक्षको जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको पुनः नियुक्तिका लागि गुठियार, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि, विभिन्न संघसंस्था र बुद्धिजीवीहरूले एकमत सिफारिस गरेका थिए । स्थानीयका अनुसार लामा सबैले स्वीकार गरेका र समन्वयकारी क्षमता भएका व्यक्ति हुन् । अध्यक्ष नहुँदा बौद्धनाथमा प्रशासनिक कामदेखि सामाजिक, धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा विकास निर्माणका गतिविधि प्रभावित भएका छन् । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिले यहाँका विभिन्न धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक संघसंस्थाबीच समन्वय गर्दै आएको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका पनि अहिले नेतृत्व अभावकै कारण कमजोर बनेको छ ।

अलमलमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा

अध्यक्षमा नियुक्ति भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र नपाउँदा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा अन्योलमा परेका छन् । नियुक्ति भइसकेको व्यक्तिलाई नै बदर गराएर अर्को व्यक्तिलाई ल्याउने प्रयास सांसद पाण्डेले गरिरहेको स्थानीयको आरोप छ ।

उनीहरू भन्छन्, ‘सर्वस्वीकार्य व्यक्तिको नियुक्ति रोक्नु सरकारकै लागि ‘ब्याकफायर’ हुन सक्छ ।’ यसअघि पनि सरकार विभिन्न नियुक्ति र निर्णयका कारण विवादमा परिसकेको छ । धार्मिक तथा सांस्कृतिक संस्थामा राजनीतिक भागबन्डा होइन, योग्य र सबैले स्वीकार गर्ने व्यक्तिलाई नेतृत्व दिनुपर्ने स्थानीयको जोड छ । यही विषयलाई लिएर काठमाडौं–३ का सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे र संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्री खडकराज पौडेल ९गणेश० बीच पनि मतभेद उत्पन्न भएको बताइएको छ ।

समितिका पाँच सदस्यमा विशाल लामा, निर्भिक्ता थिङ लामा, सेनाङ ग्याम्जो तामाङ, रोशनकुमार श्रेष्ठ र मणिभद्र पोखरेल नियुक्त भइसकेका छन् । तर अध्यक्षको नियुक्तिपत्र अझै रोकिँदा बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति नेतृत्वविहीन अवस्थामै अल्झिएको छ र राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेपको आरोप झन् गहिरिँदै गएको छ ।

articles.title: पूजारी भन्छन्– बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको भ्रमले दर्शनार्थी घटे
articles.summary:
म्याग्दी । म्याग्दीको बेनी नगरपालिका ९ स्थित देशकै ऐतिहासिक र धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको गलेश्वरधाममा यस वर्षको साउन महिनामा विगतका वर्षको तुलनामा भक्तजनको चहलपहलमा कमि आएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यताका कारण पनि दर्शनार्थीहरुको कमी आएको हो ।

साउन महिना भगवान शिवको अत्यन्त प्रिय महिना भएकाले यस अवधिमा शिवको आराधना, रुद्राभिषेक, बेलपत्र चढाउने तथा जल चढाउनु विशेष फलदायी मानिन्छ । तर बृहस्पति अन्ध भएकै कारण मन्दिरमा दर्शन गर्न हुँदैन भन्ने भ्रम फैलिएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यतालाई लिएर दर्शनसमेत गर्न नहुने भन्ने भ्रमका कारण भक्तजनको संख्या घटेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालयका गलेश्वरधामका मूल पुजारी चन्द्रमणि आचार्यका अनुसार धार्मिक शास्त्रमा भगवानको दर्शन र पूजा–अर्चना गर्न कुनै निषेध गरिएको छैन । बरु साउन महिनामा शिवको आराधना गर्दा विशेष पुण्य प्राप्त हुने धार्मिक विश्वास छ ।

गलेश्वरधाममा रहेको प्राकृतिक शिलामाथि अवस्थित स्वयं प्रकट शिवलिङ्ग विशेष आकर्षणको केन्द्र हो । एउटै ९ रोपनी क्षेत्रफलको विशाल चट्टानमाथि रहेको यो शिवलिङ्ग देश–विदेशका भक्तजनका लागि श्रद्धाको केन्द्र बनेको छ ।

विशेषगरी साउन महिना, महाशिवरात्रि, बालाचतुर्दशी तथा तीजका अवसरमा यहाँ हजारौँ श्रद्धालुको भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ ।

धेरै धार्मिक स्थलहरुमा पछि स्थापना गरिएको शिवलिङ्गमा पुजा गरिन्छ भने गलेश्वरधाममा स्वयं उत्पत्ती ज्योतिर्लिङ्ग भएको हुँदा पनि यस स्थानको छुट्टै धार्मिक महत्व हुने बताइन्छ ।

साउनको दोस्रो सोमबार भक्तजनले चढाएको भेटी गणना गरी बेनीस्थित गरिमा विकास बैंकमा दाखिला गरिएको छ । पहिलो सोमबार करिब दुई लाख रुपैयाँ भेटी संकलन भएको गलेश्वरधाममा दोस्रो सोमबार पनि करिब सोही हाराहारी रकम संकलन भएको थियो । भक्तजनको संख्या केही घटे पनि धार्मिक आस्थाका साथ दर्शन गर्ने क्रम भने निरन्तर भइरहेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र परिसरमा निर्माण गरिएको १०८ शिवलिङ्ग भक्तजनका लागि अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण बनेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र विकास कोषका उपाध्यक्ष बमबहादुर पुनको अगुवाइमा चन्दा तथा सहयोगबाट संकलित करिब साढे १३ लाख रुपैयाँमध्ये साढे ७ लाख रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर शिवलिङ्ग निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

२०७६ सालमा निर्माण गरीएको यो धार्मिक महत्व दिने आकृति एकै स्थानमा १०८ शिवलिङ्गको दर्शन र पूजा गर्न सकिने भएपछि दैनिक रूपमा भक्तजन पुग्ने गरेका छन् ।

धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक र प्राकृतिक सम्पदाको अनुपम संगमका रूपमा रहेको गलेश्वरधामले म्याग्दीको धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धनमा समेत महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ । २०८२ सालका चार वटा सोमबार गरी झण्डै १७ लाख रुपियाँ भेटी संकलन भएको थियो ।

articles.title: बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकामा भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा शुरु
articles.summary:
दोलखा । नेपालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहबाटै भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको ११ वर्षपछि दोलखाको बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकाले जिल्लामै पहिलो पटक भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखामार्फत मालपोत र नापीसम्बन्धी सेवा सञ्चालनमा ल्याएको छ ।

अब नागरिकले आफ्नै पालिकाबाट भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा पाउने भएका छन् । २०७२ सालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहलाई भूमिसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने अधिकार दिएको थियो ।

त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न नेपाल सरकारको भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी तथा गरिबी निवारण मन्त्रालय तथा संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले इच्छुक स्थानीय तहबाट आवेदन माग गरेपछि बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिका छनोटमा परेको हो ।

आवश्यक तयारी पूरा गरेपछि भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालय दोलखाले सेवा हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ । भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखा सञ्चालनसँगै जग्गा किनबेच, नामसारी, अंशबण्डा, दानपत्र, हकछोड, सट्टापट्टा, नक्सा प्रिन्ट, कित्ता रेखाङ्कन लगायतका विभिन्न सेवा चरणबद्ध रूपमा गाउँपालिकाबाटै उपलब्ध हुने जनाइएको छ ।

सेवा लिन चाहने नागरिकमध्ये डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध भइसकेकाले पालिकाबाटै सेवा लिन सक्नेछन्। डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध नभएकाले भने पहिलो पटक भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालयमा गई आफ्नो अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा दर्ता गराउनुपर्नेछ ।

नयाँ प्रणाली लागू भएसँगै सेवा नागरिकको घरदैलोमा पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिए पनि केही प्राविधिक चुनौती भने बाँकी नै छन् । भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सम्पूर्ण अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आधारित भएकाले श्रेस्ता (मूल अभिलेख) गाउँपालिकामा नहुँदा केही कानुनी तथा प्राविधिक जटिलता आउन सक्ने बताइएको छ । स्थानीय तहबाटै सेवा उपलब्ध हुन थालेपछि नागरिकको समय, खर्च र सदरमुकाम चरिकोट धाउनुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने भन्दै स्थानीय भने खुसी देखिन्छन् ।

संविधानले परिकल्पना गरेको स्थानीय तहबाट भूमि प्रशासन सेवा प्रवाहको व्यवस्था दोलखामा पनि कार्यान्वयनमा आएको हो । यसको प्रभावकारिता भने सेवा प्रवाहको गुणस्तर, डिजिटल प्रणालीको विश्वसनीयता र बाँकी प्राविधिक चुनौती समाधानमा निर्भर रहनेछ ।

articles.title: बुद्धकै पालादेखि शुरु भएको वर्षावास, किन शुरु भयो यस्तो परम्परा ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । असार पूर्णिमासँगै बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको तीन महिने वर्षावास सुरु भएको छ । गौतम बुद्धकै समयदेखि चल्दै आएको २५ सय वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आत्मअनुशासन, ध्यान, साधना र आध्यात्मिक उन्नतिको प्रतीक मानिन्छ । बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण धार्मिक परम्परा तीन महिने वर्षावास शुरु भएको छ । हरेक वर्ष असार पूर्णिमादेखि कार्तिक पूर्णिमासम्म चल्ने यो परम्परा भिक्षुहरू एकै ठाउँमा बस्ने अभ्यास मात्रै होइन, यो अनुशासन, ध्यान, आध्यात्मिक साधना र बुद्धको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष जोडिएको ऐतिहासिक अभ्यास पनि हो । बुद्धकै समयदेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्परा आखिर २५ सय वर्षपछि पनि किन उस्तै सान्दर्भिक छ ?

वर्षावासको सुरुवात

बुद्धले आफ्ना भिक्षुहरूलाई एउटा महत्वपूर्ण निर्देशन दिनुभएको थियो, “चरथ भिक्खवे चारिकं बहुजन हिताय, बहुजन सुखाय ।’ अर्थात्, “हे भिक्षुहरू ! बहुजनको हित र सुखका लागि गाउँ–गाउँ, नगर–नगर जाऊ, धर्म प्रचार गर ।’ बुद्धत्व प्राप्त गरेपछि भिक्षुहरू वर्षभरि विभिन्न स्थानमा धर्म प्रचार गर्न जान्थे । तर वर्षायाम सुरु भएपछि यात्रा कठिन हुन्थ्यो । बाटो बिग्रिन्थ्यो ।

नदीहरू बढ्थे । जीवजन्तु र बोटबिरुवामा क्षति पुग्ने सम्भावना पनि हुन्थ्यो । यही कारणले बुद्धले वर्षाको तीन महिना एकै स्थानमा बसेर ध्यान, अध्ययन र साधना गर्न निर्देशन दिनुभयो ।

यही अभ्यास नै पछि वर्षावासका रूपमा स्थापित भयो । धेरैलाई थाहा नहुन सक्छ, बौद्ध ग्रन्थमा उल्लेख भए अनुसार भगवान बुद्धले आफ्नो जीवनकालमा ४५ पटक वर्षावास बिताउनुभएको उल्लेख पाइन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष वर्षायाममा उहाँ कुनै न कुनै विहार, वन वा उपासकले बनाइदिएको आरामस्थलमा बस्नुहुन्थ्यो । यसले देखाउँछ, बुद्धले केवल उपदेश मात्र दिनुभएन । आफूले सिकाएको अभ्यासलाई जीवनभर पालना पनि गर्नुभयो ।

वर्षातको समयमा प्राकृतिक विपतिहरुबाट जोगिन र जोगाउनका साथै एकै ठाउँमा बसी नियमपुर्वक धार्मिक किसिमले जिवनयापन गर्नु नै यसको मुख्य उद्देश्य हो ।

वर्षावास किन विशेष छ ?

वर्षावास भिक्षुहरूको बसाइ मात्रै होइन । यो आत्मअनुशासनको समय हो । यस अवधिमा भिक्षुहरूले गहिरो ध्यान, विनयको अध्ययन, धर्म छलफल र आध्यात्मिक अभ्यासलाई प्राथमिकता दिन्छन् । उता गृहस्थ उपासक–उपासिकाहरू पनि विहारमा पुगेर दान, शील, ध्यान र धर्मश्रवणमार्फत आफ्नो आध्यात्मिक जीवनलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने प्रयास गर्छन् ।

वर्षावासपछि आउने कथिना चिवरदान

वर्षावास सकिएपछि बौद्ध समाजमा अर्को महत्वपूर्ण परम्परा सुरु हुन्छ कथिन चिवरदान । तीन महिना अनुशासित जीवन बिताएका भिक्षुहरूलाई श्रद्धालुहरूले सामूहिक रूपमा चिवर अर्पण गर्छन् । बौद्ध परम्परामा यसलाई सबैभन्दा ठूलो सामूहिक दानमध्ये एक मानिन्छ । यसले भिक्षु र गृहस्थबीचको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने विश्वास गरिन्छ ।

बाइट–भिक्षु कौन्डण्य, विहार प्रमुख, बुद्ध विहार

विशेषगरी यो समयमा बौद्धमार्गीहरु विभिन्न विहारमा गई बुद्ध, धर्म, संघको गुणानुस्मरण गरी ध्यान भावना गरी आध्यात्मिक उन्नती तर्फ अग्रसर हुने गर्दछन् । विशेषगरी थेरवाद बुद्धधर्मको प्रभाव रहेको मुलुकमा वर्षावास परम्पराले धार्मिक आध्यात्मिक क्षेत्रमा सकारात्मक प्रभाव पारेको कारणले यसलाई बुद्धकालिन समयदेखि अहिलेसम्म पनि निरन्तरता दिइरहेको छ ।

२५ सय वर्षदेखि नटुटेको परम्परा

विश्वका धेरै धार्मिक अभ्यास समयसँगै परिवर्तन भएका छन् । तर वर्षावास भने बुद्धकालदेखि आजसम्म मूल स्वरूपमै कायम छ । नेपाल, श्रीलंका, थाइल्याण्ड, म्यानमार, कम्बोडिया, लाओस लगायत थेरवाद बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बी देशहरूमा आज पनि लाखौं भिक्षुहरू वर्षायाममा एकै स्थानमा बसेर यही परम्परा निर्वाह गर्छन् । समय फेरियो । प्रविधि फेरियो, समाज फेरियो । तर ध्यान, अनुशासन र आत्मशुद्धिको मूल्य कहिल्यै फेरिएन । सायद यही कारणले वर्षावास आज पनि उत्तिकै जीवित र सान्दर्भिक बनेको छ । बुद्धले सुरु गर्नुभएको वर्षावास अहिले एउटा धार्मिक अनुष्ठानमा मात्रै सिमित छैन ।

यो आत्मसंयम, करुणा, अनुशासन र आध्यात्मिक विकासको तीन महिने यात्राको रुपमा समेत स्थापित भइसकेको छ । बुद्धकै पालादेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्पराले आज पनि संसारभरका लाखौं बौद्ध अनुयायीलाई ध्यान, धर्म र आत्मपरिवर्तनतर्फ प्रेरित गरिरहेको छ ।

articles.title: घरभाडा व्यवस्थापन अब डिजिटल : घरधनी र भाडावालाको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्न ‘भाडासेवा’ बजारमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालमा घर, फ्ल्याट, सटर तथा व्यावसायिक भवनको व्यवस्थापनलाई डिजिटल बनाउने उद्देश्यले एजिनेक्स क्लाउडले ‘भाडासेवा’ नामक क्लाउड–आधारित प्रणाली सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। ‘व्यवस्थित र सुमधुर सम्बन्धका लागि भाडासेवा’ मूल नारासहित आएको यो प्रणालीले कागजी अभिलेख र एक्सेल फाइलको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्दै घरभाडा व्यवस्थापनका सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रियालाई एकै डिजिटल प्लेटफर्ममा समेटेको छ।

यस प्रणालीमार्फत प्रयोगकर्ताले भवन तथा कोठाहरुको रियल–टाइम अनुगमन, भाडावालाको डिजिटल प्रोफाइल, अनलाइन सम्झौता र डिजिटल हस्ताक्षर गर्न सक्नेछन्। साथै, मासिक भाडा र बिजुली–पानीको बिल स्वतः तयार हुने, अनलाइन भुक्तानी गर्न मिल्ने तथा स्वचालित रसिद आउने सुविधा यसमा रहेको छ।

अपार्टमेन्ट तथा व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्सका साझा खर्च (CAM) व्यवस्थापन, मर्मतसम्भार ट्र्याकिङ, कर्मचारी व्यवस्थापन र आम्दानी–खर्चको विस्तृत रिपोर्टिङसमेत यसैबाट गर्न सकिन्छ।

साना घरधनीदेखि ठूला सपिङ मल र व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्ससम्मका लागि उपयोगी यो प्रणाली कम्प्युटर, ट्याब्लेट र मोबाइलबाटै सजिलै चलाउन सकिन्छ।

articles.title: इनड्राइभ नेपालद्वारा ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ प्रमाणपत्र प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं, नेपाल । विश्वव्यापी मोबिलिटी तथा डेलिभरी प्लेटफर्म इनड्राइभले महिलालाई ड्राइभिङ पेसामा अघि बढ्न समान अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरेको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रमको पहिलो चरण सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेको छ ।

कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत काठमाडौंमा आयोजित प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा तीन महिनाको प्रशिक्षण पूरा गरेका १० जना महिलालाई सम्मान गरिएको छ । सुरक्षित र आत्मनिर्भर रूपमा दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारी चलाउने पेसामा अघि बढ्न आवश्यक सीप, आत्मविश्वास र स्रोतसाधन प्रदान गर्ने उद्देश्यले सहभागीहरूलाई विभिन्न चरणमा प्रशिक्षण दिइएको थियो ।

अप्रिल २०२६ मा सुरु भएको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रम विशेषगरी अवसरबाट वञ्चित समुदायका महिलालाई मोबिलिटी क्षेत्रमा आर्थिक अवसरमा पहुँच दिलाउने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरिएको हो । महिलालाई परम्परागत रूपमा पुरुषको वर्चस्व रहेको पेसामा प्रवेश गर्न बाधा पु¥याउने सामाजिक तथा व्यावहारिक अवरोधलाई कम गर्न पनि कार्यक्रमले जोड दिएको छ ।

प्रशिक्षण अवधिभर सडक सुरक्षालाई व्यावसायिक दक्षताको महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । सहभागीहरूलाई व्यावहारिक राइडिङ प्रशिक्षणसँगै सडक सुरक्षासम्बन्धी मार्गदर्शन प्रदान गर्नुका साथै औपचारिक सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र (लाइसेन्स) प्राप्त गर्ने प्रक्रियामा समेत सहयोग गरिएको थियो ।

प्रत्येक सहभागीलाई सुरक्षात्मक हेल्मेट तथा प्राथमिक उपचार र स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी सामग्रीसहितको सुरक्षा किट प्रदान गरिएको थियो ।

व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षालाई पनि प्रशिक्षणको छुट्टै महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । फाइटब्याक नेपाल सँगको सहकार्यमा उन्नत आत्मरक्षा तालिम सञ्चालन गरिएको थियो, जसले सहभागीहरूलाई सम्भावित सुरक्षा चुनौती पहिचान गर्न, आत्मविश्वास बढाउन र आवश्यक अवस्थामा व्यवहारिक रूपमा सामना गर्न सक्ने सीप विकास गर्न सहयोग गरेको थियो ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यका ट्राफिक प्रहरी कार्यालयका डीएसपी सुनिलजंग शाहले भने, “सडक सुरक्षा सबैको साझा जिम्मेवारी हो र यसमा प्रत्येक चालकको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका हुन्छ । हामी सहभागीहरूलाई ट्राफिक नियमको पालना गर्न, सडकमा सधैं सचेत रहन र अनुभव बढाउँदै निरन्तर सिकिरहन आग्रह गर्छौं । सबै सहभागीलाई बधाई दिँदै व्यावसायिक चालकका रूपमा उनीहरूको सुरक्षित र सफल यात्राका लागि शुभकामना व्यक्त गर्दछौं ।”

मोबिलिटीमा महिलाको पहुँच विस्तार यस समूहका महिलाका लागि सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र केवल आम्दानीको माध्यम मात्र नभई आफ्नो काम, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य सेवा तथा बजारसम्म आफ्नै समयअनुसार स्वतन्त्र रूपमा पुग्ने अवसर पनि हो । यसले सार्वजनिक यातायातको समयतालिका वा परिवारका अन्य सदस्यमा निर्भर रहनुपर्ने अवस्थालाई कम गर्न सहयोग पु¥याउँछ ।

दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारीमा आधारित राइड–हेलिङ सेवाले चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारी पुग्न कठिन हुने साँघुरा गल्ली तथा अन्तिम गन्तव्यसम्म पनि सेवा पु¥याउन सक्छ । सामान्यतया यसको भाडा पनि चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारीको तुलनामा कम हुने गर्दछ । राइड–हेलिङ सेवामा महिलाको सहभागिता बढ्दा यात्रुहरूले आफूलाई उपयुक्त चालक छनोट गर्ने थप अवसरसमेत पाउनेछन् ।

प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोह प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा साझेदार संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि, सरकारी निकायका सरोकारवाला, सञ्चारकर्मी तथा विशिष्ट अतिथिहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो ।

समारोहमा इनड्राइभका प्रतिनिधि तथा इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले कार्यक्रम सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेका १० जना सहभागीलाई प्रमाणपत्र, सुरक्षा किट तथा मायाको चिनो प्रदान गरे । कार्यक्रममा सहभागी १० जना महिलाको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ यात्रालाई समेटिएको भिडियोसमेत प्रदर्शन गरिएको थियो ।

समारोहका क्रममा सहभागीमध्ये एक जनालाई विद्युतीय स्कुटर, तीन जनालाई स्मार्टफोन र छ जनालाई स्मार्टवाच प्रदान गरिएको थियो । यी सामग्रीले उनीहरूलाई व्यावसायिक ड्राइभिङ यात्राको सुरुवातमा थप सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।

इनड्राइभ साउथ एसियाकि कम्युनिकेसन म्यनाजर शेरिन एर्विना कौरले भनिन्, “हामीले विभिन्न बजारमा एउटै अवस्था देखिरहेका छौं, राइड माग्ने यात्रुमध्ये धेरै महिला छन्, तर उनीहरूलाई राइड दिने चालकमा महिलाको संख्या निकै कम छ । यो महिलाले यस्तो काम गर्न चाहन्छन् कि चाहँदैनन् भन्ने विषय थिएन। मुख्य प्रश्न उनीहरूका लागि यो पेसामा प्रवेश गर्ने बाटो उपलब्ध थियो कि थिएन भन्ने थियो । नेपालमा सञ्चालन गरिएको पहिलो समूहले तालिम, लाइसेन्स र प्लेटफर्ममा पहुँचलाई एउटै यात्राका रूपमा जोड्दा कस्तो परिवर्तन सम्भव हुन्छ भन्ने देखाएको छ। हामी अन्य बजारमा पनि यसबाट सिक्दै कार्यक्रमलाई अघि बढाउनेछौं ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी कम्युनिकेसन्स म्यानेजर मञ्जिता गुरुङले भनिन्, “सीप विकास तालिम यस यात्राको एउटा हिस्सा मात्र हो । सामाजिक सोच र धारणाले पनि उत्तिकै महत्व राख्छ, र महिलाले ड्राइभिङ सुरु गरेपछि उनी प्रवेश गर्ने वातावरण पनि महत्वपूर्ण हुन्छ । ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलालाई लाइसेन्स प्राप्त गर्नेदेखि आत्मविश्वास विकास गर्ने, परिवारमा यसबारे संवाद गर्ने र आम्दानीको अवसर सिर्जना गर्नेसम्म हरेक पक्षमा सहयोग गर्ने गरी तयार गरिएको हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरू यो पेसामा आउँछन्, यात्रुहरूले पनि लाभ पाउँछन्, उनीहरूसँग आफूलाई राइड गराउने चालक छनोट गर्ने थप विकल्प हुन्छ ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी सिनियर ड्राइभर अपरेसन्स स्पेसलिस्ट सुनिता जीमी राईले भनिन्, “इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलाका लागि थप सहयोगी वातावरण निर्माण गर्ने दिशामा महत्वपूर्ण कदम हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरूले सवारीको स्टेयरिङ समाउँछन्, उनीहरूले नेपाललाई थप समावेशी भविष्यतर्फ अघि बढाउन पनि भूमिका खेलिरहेका हुन्छन् ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले भनिन्, “‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ ले अन्यायलाई चुनौती दिँदै समुदायमा सकारात्मक परिवर्तन ल्याउने इनड्राइभको प्रतिबद्धतालाई प्रतिबिम्बित गर्छ । मानिस र समानतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर अघि बढाइएको यस पहलको हिस्सा बन्न पाउँदा म गर्व गर्छु ।”

articles.title: पार्टी निर्माणमा सि जिनपिङको अवधारणाबारे नेपालमा चर्चा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित विश्वमा राजनीतिक दलको निर्माण र त्यसको प्रभावकारी संचालनका लागि चिनियाँ राष्ट्रपति सि जिनपिङको अवधारणा उपयोगी हुने विज्ञहरुले बताएका छन् । फ्रेन्डस अन क्लाउडले काठमाडौंमा गरेको कार्यक्रममा राजनीतिज्ञ जगन्नाथ खतिवडा, परराष्ट्रविद डा गोपाल खनाल, पूर्व राजदूत महेशराज दाहाल, अनुसन्धानकर्ता डा। दीपक देवकोटा र क्लाउडका अध्यक्ष शोभित उप्रेतीले पार्टी निर्माणमा राष्ट्रपति सी का विभिन्न आयामबारे धारणा राखेका हुन् ।

कार्यक्रममा बो्ल्दै पूर्व राजदूत दाहालले राष्ट्रपति सिको अध्ययनशिल बानी नै पार्टी र राष्ट्र निर्माणका लागि आधारशिला बनेको उल्ले गरे ।

दाहालका अनुसार श्रम शिविरमा हुँदा पनि निकै अध्धयन गर्ने सी लामो र नयाँ सोचका थिए । सृजनशीलता परिवर्तनकारी सोचका धनी सीले पार्टी सदसयता पाउन पनि निकै संघर्ष गरेकाले पार्टी कस्तो हुनुपर्छ भन्ने पनि उनले राम्रोसँग बुझेका थिए ।

राम्रो दृष्टिकोण भए पार्टी र देश बन्छ भन्ने कुरा उनले प्रमाणित गरेर देखाए । भ्रष्टाचार विरुद्वका कार्यक्रम र दल भित्रको शुद्वतामा उनको जोड थियो । नेतृत्वको जिम्मेवारी र कर्तव्य । प्रविधि विकास, जनताको सहभागीता, विज्ञानमा लगानी उनको पार्टी निर्माणका प्रमुख साधन हुन ।

यस्तै , डा दिपक देवकोटाले राष्ट्रपति सीले राज्यबाट डर नभई भरोसा जगाउने काम गरेर सफलता प्राप्त गरेको धारणा राखे । जनतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर पार्टी र देश निर्माण गर्न उनी सफल भए ।

जनताले विश्वास गर्ने पार्टी बनाउन राष्ट्रपति सी ले सुशासन र सुरक्षालाई प्राथमिकता दिएको उनले बताए । परराष्ट्र विद डा गोपाल खनालले विश्वव्यापी सुशासन अभियान र नयाँ युगका लागि चिनियाँ विशेषतासहितको समाजवाद नै सि जिनपिङको पार्टी निर्माणको स्पष्ट अवधारणा भएको बताए ।

पार्टी नियम र देश कानुनबाट चल्छ भन्ने कुरा राष्ट्रपति सी ले स्थापित गरेको उनको भनाइ छ । जनतालाई विकास दिने सोच नै सिको सोच भएको खनालको निष्कर्ष छ।

आर्थिक अनियमितता गर्ने ७० लाख भन्दा बढीलाई चीनमा कारबाही गरिएको जानकारी दिंदै खनालले राष्ट्रपति सी को सुशासन अभियानको प्रशंसा गरे ।

नेता जगन्नाथ खतिवडाले अनुशासन, अनुगमन र आत्मसमीक्षाको सुत्र न‌ै राष्ट्रपति सि को पार्टी र देश निर्माणको आधारशिला रहेको धारणा राखे ।

राष्ट्रपति सि ले विचार निर्माण, राजनीति निर्माण र संगठन निर्माणमा जोड दिंदै पार्टीमा गुणस्तरीय सदस्यलाई मात्र स्थान दिएको खतिवडाले बताए । चीन जस्तो शक्तिशाली राष्ट्र हाम्रो छिमेकी भएकाले दलीय एकता तथा दीर्घकालीन सोच र योजनाका साथ अघि बढ्ने कुरा नेपालले सिक्नुपर्ने खतिवडा बताउँछन् ।

articles.title: ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंकमा नागरिक एपबाटै खाता खोल्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक लिमिटेडले नागरिक एपसँगको सहकार्यमा नागरिक एपमार्फतै बैंक खाता खोल्न सकिने नयाँ सुविधा सुरु गरेको छ ।

राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्रका आधारमा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध नेपाली नागरिकले बैंकको वेबसाइटमा उपलब्ध क्यूआर कोड स्क्यान गरी व्यक्तिगत बचत खाता अनलाइनबाटै खोल्न सक्नेछन् ।

यो सेवा १८ वर्ष वा सोभन्दा माथिका राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र भएका तथा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध व्यक्तिका लागि उपलब्ध हुनेछ । खाता खोल्ने क्रममा बैंकले ग्राहकको पूर्वसहमतिमा आवश्यक व्यक्तिगत विवरण नागरिक एपबाट सुरक्षित रूपमा प्राप्त गर्ने भएकाले पुनः विवरण भर्नुपर्ने झन्झट हट्ने, गोपनीयता कायम रहने र सूचनाको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित हुने बैंकले जनाएको छ ।

नागरिक एपमार्फत खोलिएको खाता सञ्चालनका लागि भने ग्राहकले नजिकको शाखामा गई वा भिडियो केवाईसीमार्फत प्रमाणीकरण गर्नुपर्नेछ ।

बैंकका अनुसार सरकारी डिजिटल पूर्वाधारको उपयोग गर्दै सुरु गरिएको यो सेवाले खाता खोल्ने प्रक्रियालाई थप सहज, सुरक्षित, पारदर्शी र प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनेछ । ग्राहकलाई आधुनिक डिजिटल बैंकिङ अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास बैंकको छ ।

ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक ७७ वटै जिल्लामा शाखा सञ्जाल विस्तार गर्ने निजी क्षेत्रको पहिलो वाणिज्य बैंक हो ।

हाल बैंकले ३४२ शाखा, ३६८ एटिएम, १४७ शाखारहित बैंकिङ सेवा, ६९ एक्सटेन्सन तथा राजस्व सङ्कलन काउन्टर र ३ वटा वैदेशिक प्रतिनिधि कार्यालयसहित १ हजारभन्दा बढी सेवा केन्द्रमार्फत सेवा दिँदै आएको छ ।

articles.title: मेलम्चीमा स्थानीय उत्पादन प्रवर्द्धनका लागि ‘कोशेली घर’ उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
मेलम्ची । स्थानीय कृषि र हस्तकला उत्पादनलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने उद्देश्यले सिन्धुपाल्चोकको मेलम्ची बजारमा नयाँ व्यावसायिक केन्द्र “कोशेली घर” सञ्चालनमा आएको छ। साउन ८ देखि हरेक दिन बिहान ७ बजेदेखि राति ७ बजेसम्म खुल्ने यो कोशेलीघरको उद्घाटन नगरप्रमुख आइतमान तामाङले गरेका छन् ।

नगरप्रमुख तामाङले कोशेलीघरबाट ताजा फलफूल तथा तरकारी, घरेलु अचार, मह, भान्साका आवश्यक परिकार, हस्तकला सामग्री, अण्डा, माछा, गेडागुडी, चिया, कफी तथा हर्बल सामग्रीलगायत स्थानीय रैथाने उत्पादनको सीधा बिक्री वितरणमा जोड दिने बताए । उनले यहाँ राखिने विशेष परिकार तथा उत्पादनहरू आवश्यक परेमा जिल्ला बाहिर पनि पठाइने समेत जनाए ।

कोशेलीघरले स्थानीय उत्पादक र उपभोक्तालाई एउटै छानामुनि प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाटको व्यवस्था गराउँदै बजारसम्म पहुँच सहज बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको प्रमुख तामाङले बताए ।

साथै प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत निमेष मिश्रले ‘फार्म देखि किचनसम्म अवधारणाअनुरूप उत्पादक र उपभोक्ताको मागअनुसार नयाँ वस्तु तथा उत्पादनहरू परिष्कृत गरी सार्वजनिक गरिने र उद्यमीहरूको भेटघाट हुने उपयुक्त स्थलको रूपमा यसलाई विकास गर्ने योजना रहेको बताए । प्रारम्भिक अनुमान अनुसार नगरपालिकाले दैनिक हजारौंले यहाँबाट किनमेल गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

मेलम्ची आसपासका सरकारी तथा निजी कार्यालयका कर्मचारी, घुम्न आउने पर्यटक, स्थानीय टोल तथा छिमेकी पालिकाका बासिन्दाहरू प्रमुख लक्षित ग्राहक रहने कोशेलीघरबाट स्थानिय रोजगारी र व्यवसायिक गतिविधिलाई थप सक्रिय बनाउन मद्दत पुग्ने उपस्थित उपभोक्ताले विश्वास व्यक्त गरिएको थियो ।

articles.title: २४ औं अनसन शुरु, समर्थनसँगै विरोध पनि बढ्दै
articles.summary:
कैलाली । धनगढीस्थित कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशालामा डा. गोविन्द केसीको सत्याग्रह दोस्रो दिन पनि जारी छ । स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र सुधारका पाँचबुँदे माग अघि सार्दै उनले शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय र चिकित्सा शिक्षा आयोगमा स्वार्थ बाझिने नियुक्ति खारेज गर्न, चिकित्सा शिक्षा ऐन संशोधन गर्न, छात्रवृत्ति कटौतीको निर्णय फिर्ता लिन र मापदण्ड नपुगेका निजी मेडिकल कलेजमा थप सिट स्वीकृति रोक्न सरकारसँग माग गरेका छन् ।

विगतका सहमति कार्यान्वयन, चिकित्सा शिक्षालाई गैरनाफामूलक बनाउने तथा भ्रष्टाचार र अपराधका आरोपमाथि निष्पक्ष अनुसन्धानको मागसमेत डा. केसीले गरेका छन् । डा. केसीले आफू विश्वविद्यालयको विरोधमा नभई स्वार्थ बाँझिने नियुक्तिको विरोधमा सत्याग्रहमा बसेको स्पष्ट पारेका छन् ।

यता शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय संघर्ष समितिले भने डा. केसीलाई सत्याग्रह स्थगित गर्न आग्रह गरेको छ ।

संयोजक लोकराज पाण्डेको नेतृत्वमा प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीलाई भेटेको टोलीले आन्दोलनका कारण विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालन र विकासको प्रक्रिया प्रभावित हुन सक्ने भन्दै आवश्यक पहल गर्न अनुरोध गरेको हो ।

उता, कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशाला व्यवस्थापन समितिले पूर्वसूचना बिना अनिश्चितकालीन सत्याग्रह सुरु गरिएको भन्दै डा. केसीलाई स्थान खाली गर्न पत्र दिएको छ । तर डा. केसीले व्यवस्थापन समितिसँग सहमतिमै सत्याग्रह सुरु गरेको दाबी गर्दै केही स्वार्थ समूहले आन्दोलन कमजोर पार्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको आरोप लगाए ।

उनले दबाब र अवरोधका बाबजुद आफ्ना मागबाट पछि नहट्ने र आवश्यक परे फुटपाथमै बसेर पनि सत्याग्रहलाई निरन्तरता दिने बताएका छन् ।

चिकित्सा शिक्षा सुधारको मागसँगै डा. केसीको आन्दोलन जारी रहँदा विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालनमा असर पर्ने चिन्ता भने स्थानीय स्तरमा बढ्दै गएको छ ।

articles.title: २ लाख ऋण, १४ लाख तिर्दापनि जग्गा बैंकको कब्जामा !
articles.summary:
सप्तरी । सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर–६ मा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारीका अध्यक्षले ऋणीहरूको धितो जग्गा फिर्ता नगरी आफ्नै परिवारको नाममा नामसारी गरेर बैंकमा धितो राखेको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि पीडितहरू ठगीको तथ्य थाहा पाएसँगै जग्गा फिर्ता र दोषीमाथि कारबाहीको माग गर्दै न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारीरहेका छन् ।

सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर गाउँपालिका–६ रञ्जितपुरकी रेणु देवी दासले २०७२ सालमा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारी संस्था लिमिटेडबाट छोरीको विवाहका लागि दुई लाख रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएकी थिइन् । उनले ब्याजसहित पटक–पटक गरेर करिब १४ लाख रुपैयाँ तिरेर तीन वर्षअघि नै ऋण चुक्ता गरिन् । तर सहकारीका अध्यक्ष दिलिप यादवले घरको लालपुर्जा फिर्ता दिन आलटाल गर्दै आएका छन् ।

अहिले मल्टीपर्पस् फाइनान्स बैंकले उक्त घरजग्गा लिलामीको सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि सहकारी अध्यक्षको कर्तुत सार्वजनिक भएको छ भने पीडित परिवार न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारिएको छ । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा सहकारीका अध्यक्ष यादवले जग्गा आफ्नो पत्नी सुनिता यादवको नाममा नामसारी गराई सोही जग्गा धितो राखेर बैंकबाट ऋण लिएको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना जारी गरेपछि मात्रै पीडितले आफ्नो जग्गा अर्कैको नाममा रहेको थाहा पाएका हुन् ।

लिलामी सूचना देखेपछि रेणु दास बैंक पुगेर आफ्नो जग्गाबारे जानकारी मागेकी थिइन् । बैंकले ऋण बराबरको रकम तिरेपछि मात्रै जग्गा फिर्ता गर्न सकिने जनाएको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यसपछि उनले सहकारी अध्यक्षलाई बैंक जान आग्रह गरे पनि उनले अस्वीकार गर्दै सम्पर्कबाट टाढिएका छन् ।

यस्तै स्थानीय पुलकित मुखियाले पनि ५० हजार रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएर धितो राखेको एक कठ्ठा जग्गा ऋण चुक्ता गर्दा समेत फिर्ता नपाएको र आफ्नो नामबाटै नामसारी गरिएको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

पीडितहरू सहकारीका सञ्चालकले सम्पत्ति बेचेर फरार हुने आशंकामा छन् । उनीहरू आफ्नो जग्गा फिर्ता गराइ दोषीमाथि कारबाही गर्न सम्बन्धित निकायसँग न्यायको माग गरिरहेका छन् ।

articles.title: उजाड पाखामा चिया खेती, गाउँमै रोजगारी
articles.summary:
दोलखा । दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–४ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँमै रोजगारी सिर्जना गरेको छ । बाँझो जमिन हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र युवाले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गर्दै स्थानीय आर्थिक गतिविधिमा उल्लेख्य टेवा पु¥याएका छन् ।

दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–९ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँको स्वरूप फेरिएको छ । रोजगारीको अभावका कारण हुने युवा पलायन र बाँदर आतंकजस्ता समस्याको समाधान गर्दै चिया खेती स्थानीयका लागि आयआर्जनको भरपर्दो माध्यम बनेको छ ।

पहिले उत्तिसको घारीले ढाकिएको र झुसुले किराको समस्याले विद्यालयका विद्यार्थीसमेत प्रभावित थिए । तर यो क्षेत्र वडा कार्यालयको पहलमा सफा गरी इलामबाट ल्याइएका २५ हजार चियाका बिरुवासहित हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण गरिएको छ ।

प्रारम्भिक परीक्षण सफल भएपछि यसको व्यवस्थापनको जिम्मा स्थानीयको सहभागितामा बनेको सुन्द्रावती चिया विकास समूहलाई हस्तान्तरण गरिएको छ । ७–८ वर्षको अन्तरालमा यहाँ उत्पादित चियाले बजार पाउन थालेको छ ।

प्रति किलो १०० रुपैयाँका दरले चियाको मुना टिप्ने व्यवस्था भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र परीक्षा दिएर बसेका विद्यार्थीले गाउँमै रोजगारी पाएका छन् । बिहानदेखि साँझसम्म काम गर्ने मजदुरले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गरिरहेका छन् ।

वडा कार्यालयको बजेट र लगानीमा अघि बढाइएको यस योजनामा चालु आर्थिक वर्ष मात्रै ४ लाख रुपैयाँ थप लगानी गरिएको छ । चिया प्रशोधन सहज बनाउन ६ लाख रुपैयाँ लागतमा तीन प्रकारका आधुनिक प्रशोधन मेसिनसमेत सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको छ ।

स्थानीय सरकारको सही योजना र निरन्तर लगानी भए बाँझो जमिनलाई पनि आम्दानीको स्रोत बनाउन सकिने उदाहरण सुन्द्रावतीको चिया खेतीले प्रस्तुत गरेको छ ।

articles.title: Delayed response, absent leadership: How Sunsari’s violence spread unchecked
articles.summary:
The government's delayed response—political and administrative—to communal violence in Dewanganj of Sunsari district has come under mounting criticism from security experts, rights advocates, opposition leaders and lawmakers. They say crucial opportunities to contain the crisis were missed, allowing tensions to spread to several districts and leaving three people dead in police firing.

The violence, which began after a dispute between two groups in Dewanganj Rural Municipality of Sunsari, has since spread to parts of Saptari, Siraha, Dhanusha and Parsa, prompting curfews, fresh protests and heightened security deployment. Police firing during the unrest has left three people dead, while the number of injured, including security personnel, has continued to rise.

Questions have also emerged over the government's handling of the crisis. Critics say Prime Minister Balendra Shah and Home Minister Sudan Gurung failed to provide timely political leadership, neglected dialogue with stakeholders and relied primarily on security measures instead of preventive intervention.

Despite the seriousness of the incident, the government did not immediately engage local representatives, federal lawmakers, provincial assembly members, political parties, civil society groups or community leaders in efforts to calm tensions.

Although the home minister convened a security meeting shortly after the violence erupted, the prime minister did not even receive a briefing from the heads of the Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force immediately. He met them only four days after the incident and convened a meeting of the National Security Council on the fifth day on Thursday.

Neither Shah nor Gurung visited the affected area or formally addressed the nation in the immediate aftermath. The home minister travelled to Sunsari only five days after the violence, while the prime minister released a video message urging restraint.

A subsequent all-party meeting held in Sunsari on Wednesday was attended by aides to the home minister and the infrastructure development minister rather than senior government officials from Kathmandu.

The government's handling has drawn particular criticism because security agencies had reportedly warned three years ago about the possibility of communal violence in the area. According to officials and security experts, authorities also failed to gather and act on local intelligence before the clashes escalated.

Former National Human Rights Commission member and advocate Mohna Ansari said the state had failed in both coordination and crisis management.

"Why did the prime minister and home minister not treat the Sunsari incident with the seriousness it demanded from the very beginning?" Ansari asked. "How did a local dispute escalate to the point where police used live ammunition? And why was there no political outreach when it was obvious that tensions could spread elsewhere?"

She argued that imposing curfews alone could not restore public confidence. "The government itself should have been actively engaged. Local representatives, political parties and community leaders should have been mobilised immediately. The further firing on Thursday and the spread of unrest show weaknesses in both coordination and follow-up," she said.

The violence began on Sunday when a dispute between two groups in Dewanganj escalated into clashes. Security forces responded with what witnesses and rights advocates described as excessive force, including the use of live ammunition.

Thirty-year-old Om Prakash Mehata of Dewanganj-4 was killed after being shot by police, while at least nine local residents sustained serious injuries.

Twenty-year-old Jay Prakash Mehta later died while undergoing treatment at Neuro Hospital in Biratnagar.

The unrest subsequently spiralled into Madhesh Province. In Golbazar, Siraha, police again opened fire after demonstrations intensified despite a daytime curfew. Seventeen-year-old Ganesh Yadav of Aurahi Rural Municipality-2 died after sustaining a gunshot wound.

Security analysts argue that the spread of violence could have been prevented had authorities responded more quickly to intelligence warnings and prioritised dialogue over force. They say security agencies concentrated on restoring order only after violence had already erupted instead of taking preventive measures through community engagement and early intervention before tensions flared across the region.

The government's political response has also come under scrutiny. As tensions escalated, critics expected Prime Minister Shah and Home Minister Gurung to convene an all-party meeting to build consensus and send a unified message against communal violence.

Instead, that initiative was taken by Rastriya Swatantra Party Chairman Rabi Lamichhane, who consulted leaders of the Nepali Congress, the CPN-UML and other parties, seeking suggestions and cooperation to restore calm. Neither the prime minister nor the home minister attended the all-party meeting, prompting criticism from both ruling and opposition lawmakers.

The issue also dominated Thursday's meeting of the House of Representatives, where members repeatedly demanded answers from the government. Although Speaker DP Aryal had reportedly advised the prime minister a day earlier to address Parliament on the deteriorating situation, neither Shah nor Gurung made a statement. Security chiefs had also suggested that Parliament be formally briefed, but lawmakers said the government remained silent despite growing public concern.

Most of the lawmakers who addressed Thursday's House of Representatives meeting questioned the absence of the prime minister and the home minister, demanding the government explain its handling of the incident.

Former prime minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal criticised what he described as the government's failure to provide political leadership at a time of crisis. "The situation seen in Sunsari, Morang and elsewhere must be resolved through dialogue and cooperation," Dahal told Parliament.

"The people must remain united against those trying to exploit divisions and make the situation worse. Although Lamichhane eventually called an all-party meeting, it was the prime minister who should have taken that initiative. His absence, along with that of the home minister, is deeply concerning."

PM Shah was expected to hold consultation with lawmakers from the affected area but that did not happen. Lamichhane held discussions with his party's lawmakers elected from Madhesh Province, urging them to play an active role in restoring communal harmony in their constituencies.

Participants complained that the government's engagement with affected communities had been inadequate and that victims' families had not received the support they expected from the state.

RSP lawmaker Deepak Kumar Sah said discussions focused on preventing further communal polarisation and identifying constructive ways for lawmakers to assist the government. Another RSP lawmaker, Manish Jha, argued that the state should first reach victims and address their concerns before relying on security measures alone. "The people responsible for running the state must respond promptly and visibly," he said.

Critics also questioned why the federal government failed to coordinate with provincial administrations, chief ministers, local governments and elected representatives despite having established mechanisms to do so.

Leaders, including Nepali Congress President Gagan Kumar Thapa and Dahal, said the extensive networks of political parties and elected representatives down to ward level could have been mobilised to appeal for calm and prevent misinformation from spreading.

Several Madhesh-based leaders, including Mahanta Thakur, Rajendra Mahato, CK Raut, Samim Ansari and former Constituent Assembly member Ram Kumar Sharma, urged restraint and warned against attempts to deliberately destabilise the Tarai-Madhesh region through communal polarisation. They demanded an impartial investigation and called for a high-level judicial inquiry led by a retired Supreme Court justice.

Questions have also been raised over the authorities' response to inflammatory content circulating on social media after the violence. Critics say security agencies failed to monitor and curb posts designed to inflame religious hatred.

Nepal Police spokesperson Abhinarayan Kafle said police had deployed teams to monitor misinformation using available technology, including an artificial intelligence desk, and promised legal action against those found spreading false or provocative content.

The incident has further exposed weaknesses within Nepal's intelligence and security apparatus. Despite previous warnings of possible communal unrest, authorities failed to assess the situation adequately or prevent escalation. The National Investigation Department, recently brought under the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, has also come under criticism over its intelligence gathering.

Compounding those concerns, key security posts in Koshi Province and Sunsari were vacant or being handled by acting officials when the violence erupted. Sunsari district police chief Superintendent Keshav Kumar Thebe and Koshi Province Police chief DIG Binod Ghimire were on leave, while the Armed Police Force's Sunsari commander had been transferred two weeks earlier.

SPs Narayan Chimoriya and Suman Timsina from the provincial police office were later dispatched to coordinate operations. Critics argue that the leadership vacuum further weakened the state's initial response and deepened public distrust.

articles.title: Violence spreads across Madhesh days after Sunsari clash, death toll rises to three
articles.summary:
Communal tensions that erupted after a dispute in Sunsari have spread in several Tarai districts, leaving three people dead, and prompting sweeping security measures across four districts.

Authorities have imposed curfew orders in Sunsari, Saptari Siraha and Dhanusha as of Thursday night, while a prohibitory order was enforced in Parsa as violence spread from the eastern district of Sunsari. Nepal Police, the Armed Police Force and the Nepali Army have been deployed in large numbers to contain the unrest.

The latest fatality was Ganesh Yadav, 17, of ward 2 in Aurahi Rural Municipality in Siraha who died after being shot during clashes in Golbazar on Thursday afternoon. Earlier in the day, Jaya Prakash Mehta, 20, who had been critically injured in Sunday’s violence in Sunsari, died while undergoing treatment at Neuro Hospital in Biratnagar. The unrest began after 24-year-old Om Prakash Mehta of ward 3 in Dewanganj Rural Municipality was shot dead on Sunday night during a confrontation between two communities in Sunsari.

Police headquarters said security forces have been instructed to prioritise crowd-control measures such as tear gas and baton charges, while maintaining dialogue with community leaders, local representatives and other stakeholders.

“We have directed personnel to use force proportionately and focus on engagement with communities to prevent further escalation,” Deputy Inspector General Abi Narayan Kafle, spokesperson for Nepal Police, told Kantipur.

The situation deteriorated rapidly in Siraha’s Golbazar after protesters defied a curfew imposed from 2pm.

Yadav had received bullet injuries in his neck, according to doctors involved in his treatment. Another victim, 19-year-old Subhash Thakur of ward 8 in Dhanushadham Municipality in Dhanusha district, suffered a gunshot wound to the back and was transferred to the BP Koirala Institute of Health Sciences in Dharan. Doctors described his condition as critical.

Police have yet to determine where the fatal shots came from—the Nepal Police, the Armed Police Force or the Nepali Army teams deployed.

“The situation remains tense,” Superintendent Ramesh Bahadur Pal, spokesperson for the District Police Office, Siraha, said. “Our immediate priority is to restore order.”

Protests had begun early Thursday morning when demonstrators blocked the East-West Highway at Kasaha before unrest spread to Golbazar. Protesters vandalised and set fire to several shops, including the AB Mall, before security forces moved in.

Residents said another group, carrying homemade weapons and travelling on around two dozen motorcycles and several auto-rickshaws, arrived in the town around midday, sharply escalating tensions.

As rival groups gathered on opposite sides of the town, security forces dispersed crowds using baton charges and 21 rounds of tear gas shells. The district administration imposed a curfew from 2pm, and the Nepali Army was deployed.

Despite the restrictions, protesters again advanced towards the highway around 3:30pm, after which security personnel opened fire, according to officials.

The shooting further inflamed the situation. Protesters torched and vandalised more than a dozen businesses.

“The town remained gripped by fear throughout the day,” said resident Surendra Sah.

Civil society leader Arjun Thapaliya blamed the violence on security failures.

“The security agencies failed to act despite protests continuing for days. They should have anticipated what was coming,” he said.

Police also fired warning shots and used tear gas in Lahan after another confrontation threatened to erupt between two communities. A curfew has also been imposed there.

Siraha Chief District Officer Surendra Paudel said the administration would review the security situation before deciding whether to expand the restrictions. He said authorities were coordinating with political parties and community representatives to prevent further violence.

Janakpur under curfew

The unrest reached Madhesh provincial headquarters of Janakpur on Thursday morning, where demonstrators shut markets and clashed repeatedly with police before authorities imposed an indefinite curfew from 3:30pm.

Chief District Officer Prem Prasad Luitel said the indefinite curfew covers all wards of Janakpurdham Sub-metropolitan City and adjoining areas extending from Laxminiya in the north to Nagarain in the south, and from the Belouni Road corridor in the east to the Sinurjoda and Dudhmati Bridge areas in the west. The administration published detailed boundary coordinates in its official order.

The district administration has also authorised the Nepali Army to use live ammunition if necessary while enforcing the curfew, instructing troops to apply only the minimum force required.

Earlier in the day, large groups of protesters moved through Janakpur, forcing businesses to close. Clashes with police broke out at Ramananda Chowk and Bajrang Chowk.

Police said several protesters were injured.

“After the curfew, the situation has begun to stabilise,” a security official in Dhanusha said. “Protesters had started targeting homes, businesses and community-specific properties, making a stronger security response necessary.”

The Nepali Army has deployed armoured vehicles, helicopters and foot patrols across Janakpur.

In Parsa district, the administration imposed prohibitory orders in sensitive parts of Birgunj from 5pm Thursday until 6am Friday.

The order bans gatherings of more than five people, demonstrations, rallies and other public assemblies. Officials warned that anyone violating the restrictions would face legal action.

The curfew covering ten local units in Sunsari, first enforced on Tuesday night, remained in effect for a third consecutive day.

Officials said the security situation had gradually improved, but the restrictions could not be lifted because negotiations with the families of those killed had yet to produce an agreement.

The body of Om Prakash Mehta remains in hospital as his family continues to refuse to collect it.

The family has demanded that he be declared a martyr, provided adequate compensation and assured that those responsible for the shooting will be prosecuted before they agree to perform his funeral rites.

Authorities have urged residents to comply with the curfew, avoid rumours and help maintain public order.

As tensions spread across the Madhesh region, Nepal Police has reinforced deployments by recalling officers from elsewhere in the country.

The police headquarters has suspended all leaves except for bereavement and maternity-related cases to ensure sufficient personnel are available in affected districts.

“We are concentrating manpower wherever the security challenge is greatest to prevent further loss of life and property,” Kafle said.

Addressing the nation on Thursday evening, Prime Minister Balendra Shah pledged an impartial investigation into the violence and said the government would take all necessary measures to restore peace.

articles.title: 17 years later, senior foreign ministry official charged over alleged misuse of travel documents
articles.summary:
In 2009, five Tibetans arrived at the German Embassy in Kathmandu carrying Nepal-issued travel documents and seeking visas to join relatives who had been granted asylum in Germany. They claimed they were recent arrivals from Tibet. But their documents soon raised a troubling question: how had newcomers to Nepal obtained official travel papers so quickly?

That question set off an investigation that exposed alleged abuse of Nepal’s travel document system, possible involvement of foreign ministry officials, hundreds of missing travel document booklets and a case that languished for years.

The case filed on Monday over passport offences alleges that Nepal’s travel document system was abused to provide government-issued papers to individuals who were not registered refugees in the country.

Investigators and prosecutors allege that five Tibetans linked to refugee camps in India were falsely portrayed as Tibetan refugees residing in Nepal to secure travel documents. The investigation has also uncovered questions over alleged financial dealings, missing government documents and why a case that came to the attention of authorities quickly took so long to reach court.

The allegations centre on foreign ministry joint secretary Pushpa Raj Bhattarai, who now heads the ministry’s Labour Migration and Nepali Diaspora Coordination Division.

Investigators allege that Bhattarai, who was serving as a section officer at the Department of Passports at the time, approved travel documents for five Tibetans from Indian refugee settlements after they were falsely portrayed as refugees residing in Nepal.

The Kathmandu District Attorney’s Office filed a passport offence case against Bhattarai on Monday, seeking imprisonment and fines based on the investigation by the Central Investigation Bureau.

Bhattarai has denied any wrongdoing. He told investigators that he did not know how the documents were prepared and that his signature may have been misused.

According to the charge sheet filed at Kathmandu District Court, Bhattarai and others illegally issued travel documents to Tibetan refugees under the pretext of family reunification, with the alleged aim of sending them to Germany.

Prosecutors have argued that the act constitutes an offence under Nepal’s passport laws.

Under the previous Passport Act of 1967, providing false statements or details to obtain a passport or allowing misuse of a passport could result in up to one year in prison or a fine. The revised Passport Act of 2019 allows a fine of Rs200,000 to Rs500,000, imprisonment of one to three years, or both for obtaining or attempting to obtain a passport or travel document through false information.

A second foreign ministry employee, then non-gazetted officer Bachhuram KC, was also found to have been allegedly involved in the process. However, prosecutors decided not to pursue charges against him because he died on August 20, 2019.

Although offices in Nepal or Nepali diplomatic missions abroad can issue travel documents to refugees residing in Nepal who have received government approval and submitted applications along with recommendations from the Ministry of Home Affairs, the charge sheet states that travel documents were issued to refugees living in camps in India based on forged documents.

The police investigation found that then-officer Bhattarai had issued travel documents, based on forged documents, in the names of Tenzin Namgyal Chungotsang (travel document no. A-026518), Tenzin Tendhar Chungotsang (A-026523), Pentsog Gongda Tsang (A-026225), Chime Gongda Tsang (A-026226), and Ngawang Gongda Tsang (A-026227).

The case filed at the court also seeks the cancellation of the travel documents issued to them.

The documents were issued by the Department of Passports on August 4 and August 14, 2009. Madhav Kumar Nepal was prime minister, Sujata Koirala was foreign minister, and Gyan Chandra Acharya was foreign secretary at the time the travel documents were issued based on allegedly forged documents.

Visa application that triggered the probe

The issue first surfaced when the five Tibetans applied for visas at the German Embassy in Kathmandu.

German consular officer Andrea Arslan became suspicious after reviewing the travel documents they had submitted. On April 2, 2010, she wrote to Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs asking it to investigate the documents instead of issuing visas.

The foreign ministry later forwarded the embassy’s letter to Nepal Police headquarters, which eventually reached the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) on July 12, 2011.

Tenzin Namgyal Chungotsang and Tenzin Tendhar Chungotsang had applied for family reunification visas on November 18, 2009. The three members of the Gongda Tsang, Pentsog Gongda Tsang, Chime Gongda Tsang, and Ngawang Gongda Tsang submitted their applications on December 23, 2009.

Both families claimed they were Tibetan refugees who had “recently” arrived from Tibet and wanted to reunite with relatives who had already received asylum in Germany.

Though DNA tests confirmed their claimed family relationships with the relatives living in Germany, German officials questioned whether their claims about their refugee status and residence history matched official records.

An investigation found that the Gongda Tsang family had been registered at the Dekyiling Tibetan settlement in Dehradun, India, since 1981. The Chungotsang family was also found to have links with the Tibetan refugee community in India.

The German Embassy also questioned why the established process under the Nepal-India understanding on Tibetan refugees had not been followed. Under the arrangement, Tibetan refugees generally process travel-related matters through the Tibetan administration in Dharamsala, India, with assistance from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

The embassy sought verification from Nepal’s foreign ministry after doubts over how the applicants obtained Nepal-issued travel documents,

The ministry confirmed that the documents had been issued by the Nepal government.

However, when the embassy sought additional details from Nepal’s Department of Immigration, it was informed that the necessary recommendation documents required for issuing such travel documents had not been submitted.

During further questioning by embassy officials, the applicants allegedly said they had paid Rs400,000 to obtain each travel document from the foreign ministry and another Rs400,000 to leave Nepal through the airport.

The allegation of financial payments was included in the German Embassy’s complaint.

However, prosecutors decided not to include the financial transaction issue in the passport offence case and instead forwarded it to the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) for separate investigation.

No record of hundreds of missing travel documents

The investigation uncovered another serious issue: hundreds of travel document booklets that disappeared from government custody.

According to investigators, Bachhuram KC, who worked in the foreign ministry’s store section, took 500 travel document booklets from the ministry’s storage facility on July 10, 2009, claiming they were meant for Nepal’s diplomatic mission in Cairo, Egypt.

But investigators later found that the Nepali mission in Cairo had never requested those documents and that no such documents had reached the mission during that period.

Where the remaining documents went remains unanswered.

Before his death, KC told the Central Investigation Bureau that he had received the 500 travel document booklets.

“Reports had appeared in various newspapers that 500 documents were missing. I personally received those documents for issuing them to the concerned individuals,” KC said in his statement.

He also acknowledged that the handwriting on travel documents issued in the names of Tibetan applicants appeared similar to his own.

According to investigators, after KC completed the administrative process, Bhattarai approved the documents.

In his statement to the CIB in January 2026, Bhattarai claimed that his signature had been misused and placed on the documents without his consent.

However, forensic examination has already confirmed that the signatures were his.

Five Tibetan refugees received travel documents bearing Bhattarai’s signature on July 4, 2009.

Investigators suspect that the documents may have been misused to issue travel papers to additional Tibetan refugees as well. However, no detailed investigation has yet been conducted.

Nepal currently hosts around 12,000 Tibetan refugees who arrived from Tibet and settled in refugee camps across 12 districts, including Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Kaski.

A case that reached court after years

The German Embassy first raised concerns about the case in 2010.

Although the matter reached the CIB a year later, the investigation failed to make significant progress for years.

During that period, governments changed, police leadership changed, and officials linked to the case continued to progress in their careers.

Bhattarai, who is now a defendant in the case, was working in the Foreign Ministry’s Consular Division from August 4, 2009, with responsibility for issuing passports and travel documents.

During its renewed investigation, the CIB recorded Bhattarai’s statement on February 6 2026. However, police didn’t arrest Bhattarai immediately. Bhattarai has been listed as a “fugitive” in the case that was filed on Monday. He, however, remains listed on the Foreign Ministry’s website as the head of his division.

After the incident, Bhattarai rose from section officer to under-secretary and then joint secretary. He served at Nepal’s diplomatic missions in South Korea and New York before eventually returning to the Foreign Ministry as a division chief.

The CIB reopened the old file in June 2025 and resumed the investigation after years of inactivity.

In his statement to investigators, Bhattarai said he joined the Foreign Ministry as a non-gazetted first-class officer in 1995, became a section officer in 2007, later served as under-secretary and was promoted to joint secretary in January 2025.

Bhattarai has maintained that he does not know how travel documents were created for Tibetan citizens using allegedly false documents.

However, the disputed travel documents carry his signature, which forensic examination has confirmed.

“My signature must have been copied by someone with wrongful intentions. Someone else may have deliberately produced signatures resembling mine,” Bhattarai told investigators.

Questions beyond five travel documents

The case is no longer limited to the five travel documents issued to Tibetan applicants.

It has raised wider questions about how refugee travel documents are managed in Nepal and whether government officials themselves have enabled the misuse of state-issued papers.

The allegations come after another major refugee-related fraud case in which government officials were accused of helping Nepali citizens obtain fake Bhutanese refugee identities and facilitating their attempted resettlement to the United States.

In that case, the Kathmandu District Court recently convicted 16 people, including former deputy prime minister Top Bahadur Rayamajhi, former home minister Balkrishna Khand and former home secretary Tek Narayan Pandey.

The court found them guilty of offences including offences against the state, fraud, forgery and organised crime.

The case involving travel documents issued in the names of Tibetan refugees will now be decided by the court.

But the investigation has left a question unanswered: why did a case first flagged by a foreign embassy remain under wraps for so long, and why did it take more than 15 years for authorities to bring it before a court?

articles.title: Extreme heat threatens Nepal's economy as warming accelerates
articles.summary:
In the scorching mid-June afternoon, as temperatures hovered around 40 degrees Celsius, 67-year-old Gopal Damai was still pulling his rickshaw through the streets of Mahendranagar in far-western Nepal.

For four decades, he has earned his living transporting goods in the three-wheeled cart. But increasingly frequent and intense heatwaves have made that livelihood harder to sustain.

“I only work in the morning and evening. I can't work during the day,” he told Kantipur Daily in May.

“Some days, I don't even earn Rs100. I have to buy vegetables on credit.”

The blistering heat has emptied Mahendranagar's streets. Fewer people venture outdoors during the day, leaving Damai with few customers and even fewer opportunities to earn.

More than 250 kilometres east, in Bardiya's Gulariya Municipality, 37-year-old Puja Bhujuwa faces a similar struggle.

She spends long hours pushing a cart and selling roasted corn near the district land revenue office.

The heat radiating from the asphalt burns her feet, while the 40-degree temperature leaves her with persistent headaches. Despite the oppressive conditions, she must keep roasting corn over a wood fire to support her family.

“Business was good until April,”Bhujuwa told Kantipur in May. “Since June, the heat has intensified, people have stopped coming out during the day, and our sales have dropped sharply.”

The hardships faced by Damai and Bhujuwa illustrate a broader trend.

Extreme heat is no longer confined to Nepal's southern Tarai. Hill towns and cities, including the Kathmandu Valley, are also experiencing steadily rising temperatures, exposing millions of workers to growing health and economic risks.

In Kathmandu, the heat is increasingly taking a toll on informal and daily wage workers who spend long hours outdoors, often without access to shade, cooling facilities or adequate drinking water.

Nepal, long regarded as a cool Himalayan country, is now emerging as one of South Asia's fastest-warming nations, according to the World Bank's 2026 report, A Livable Future: Protecting Jobs and Growth from Extreme Heat in South Asia's Cities.

The report says Nepal has already warmed by 1.26 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, making it one of the region's fastest-warming countries. Under a medium-emissions scenario, temperatures are projected to rise by another 2.8 degrees Celsius by the end of the century.

The warming will be most pronounced across the Himalayas and foothills, where rising temperatures are expected to alter regional weather patterns, increase humidity and intensify heat across the Indo-Gangetic plains.

Urban centres in Nepal's hills are also warming rapidly. Kathmandu already experiences a pronounced urban heat island effect, with temperatures in the city core reaching up to 4 degrees Celsius higher than surrounding parts of the valley because of dense construction, concrete surfaces and shrinking green spaces.

Although Kathmandu still experiences fewer days of extreme heat than many lowland South Asian cities, the report warns that warming trends indicate even high-altitude cities will increasingly face dangerous heat stress.

Between May 2024 and May 2025, Nepal recorded 89 days with temperatures above the historical 90th percentile, underscoring how quickly extreme heat is becoming the new normal.

According to the World Bank, extreme heat is steadily eroding Nepal's economic productivity by reducing workers' capacity to perform physically demanding jobs, particularly in construction, agriculture and the informal sector. Rising temperatures are also increasing electricity demand, overheating buildings and disrupting transport systems.

Poor households are expected to bear the heaviest burden. Families living in informal settlements often lack reliable electricity, cooling facilities and access to healthcare, making them especially vulnerable to prolonged heatwaves.

The report estimates that more than 700 million people across India, Bangladesh and Nepal already live in areas where outdoor heat stress exceeds safe physiological limits for at least one day every year.

The health burden is also rising rapidly across the region. Across Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Sri Lanka, deaths in which high temperatures were identified as a contributing risk factor nearly doubled between 2000 and 2023—from around 118,000 to approximately 230,000—representing an increase of about 95 percent, or an average annual rise of 4.1 percent.

The report also calls for stronger monitoring of heat-related illnesses and deaths, expanded early warning systems, greener urban planning and the adoption of heat-resilient building standards.

According to the report, embedding heat resilience into urban planning, infrastructure investment and public health systems before temperatures rise further could prevent extreme heat from becoming a long-term constraint on Nepal's economic growth and livability.

The report explains that the human body maintains an internal temperature of about 37 degrees Celsius. Physical activity generates heat, while sweating and the widening of blood vessels near the skin help cool the body. But hotter air, higher humidity and prolonged exposure to direct sunlight or heated surfaces reduce the body's ability to dissipate heat.

When those natural cooling mechanisms fail, people become vulnerable to heat exhaustion, heatstroke and other illnesses that place severe stress on the heart, lungs and kidneys, sometimes resulting in death.

Beyond the health risks, the World Bank warns that extreme heat is already weighing heavily on South Asia's economy.

The equivalent of 31 million full-time jobs are lost annually across the region as workers slow down, stop work early or fall ill. Businesses also suffer as electricity systems, transport networks and buildings struggle to function efficiently under extreme temperatures, reducing productivity, investment and economic output.

According to the report, informal workers' incomes decline by about 40 percent during a heatwave. At the same time, household spending on drinking water, cooling and healthcare rises sharply. Prolonged heat can also force families to borrow money, sell productive assets or pull children out of school to cope with financial stress.

Without adequate adaptation measures, rising temperatures could reduce South Asia's gross domestic product by nearly 7 percent by 2050, the steepest projected decline among developing regions. Shrinking tax revenues coupled with rising public spending on healthcare, energy and damaged infrastructure could create a prolonged fiscal burden for governments.

Dr Prajal Pradhan, associate professor at the Integrated Research on Energy, Environment and Society at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands, said intensifying heatwaves would affect Nepal through both public health and the economy.

“Heatwaves worsen existing illnesses, increase heat-related deaths and reduce labour productivity,” he said.

“As heatwaves become more frequent, demand for cooling will increase, and this requires more electricity. Poor ventilation in buildings also leads to overheating as temperatures rise. Extreme heat can even soften asphalt and disrupt transport systems.”

Pradhan said households living in poorly constructed homes remain highly vulnerable to both cold spells and heatwaves.

“The long-term solution is to ensure decent housing with proper heating and cooling facilities. Expanding green spaces and water bodies in urban areas can also help reduce temperatures and lessen the impact of heatwaves.”

The report said that dense urban areas can remain more than 10 degrees Celsius warmer than surrounding rural areas at night because concrete and asphalt retain heat long after sunset. The lack of nighttime cooling prevents the human body from recovering from daytime heat stress, making prolonged heat exposure even more dangerous.

By 2070, around 520 million people across South Asia are projected to experience at least one month of dangerous heat every year—four times the current number. Much of that exposure will be concentrated in cities, while the Himalayas and their foothills are expected to experience the fastest rate of warming.

The report also warns that the true death toll from extreme heat is likely far higher than official figures indicate because many fatalities are recorded as cardiac or kidney failure rather than heat-related deaths.

Economist Chandra Mani Adhikari said extreme heat is already affecting multiple sectors of Nepal's economy.

“Heatwaves have not only reduced agricultural production but have also significantly affected public health and employment,”he said. “Government and household healthcare spending has risen considerably, while disasters linked to climate change are damaging critical infrastructure.” According to Adhikari, Nepal has failed to adequately strengthen its climate adaptation programmes.

“The current trend suggests Nepal could face growing food insecurity if these problems are not properly analysed and addressed,” he said.

To reduce future losses, the World Bank proposes a broad set of interventions spanning public health, social protection, energy, transport, finance and urban planning.

It recommends investing in early warning systems, strengthening health services, protecting outdoor workers, expanding urban forests and shaded public spaces, and making electricity and transport systems more resilient to extreme heat.

“Heatwaves disrupt every part of city life, so the response must involve the whole of government,” the report says. It also calls for mobilising private investment to expand access to affordable cooling, finance green and climate-resilient buildings, improve cooling systems for industry and healthcare, and develop insurance mechanisms to manage heat-related risks.

Rather than creating entirely new programmes, the report recommends integrating heat resilience into existing initiatives. Employment schemes such as Nepal's National Employment Promotion Programme, national health systems and housing programmes could incorporate heat adaptation measures by updating operational guidelines without requiring major new spending.

The report also highlights the role of frontline community workers. Nepal's Female Community Health Volunteers could help deliver heat advisories and protect pregnant women, children and elderly people through the systems already in place.

As air-conditioning becomes more common, electricity demand is expected to shift increasingly to the evening and night because buildings retain heat after sunset and nighttime temperatures are rising faster than daytime temperatures.

The tourism sector is also expected to face growing risks.

The report recommends retrofitting heritage sites in the Kathmandu Valley—including the Durbar Squares, Pashupatinath, Bauddhanath and Swayambhunath—as well as lowland pilgrimage destinations such as Lumbini and Janakpur with shaded walkways, water features, traditional courtyard ventilation and cool-roof technologies that comply with conservation standards.

According to the report, the Nepal Tourism Board, the Department of Archaeology, UNESCO, the Asian Development Bank and private investors could jointly finance these improvements to protect tourism assets that support an industry worth around $700 million and provide employment for nearly one million people.

The report also recommends strengthening Nepal's electricity network through grid upgrades, distributed renewable energy with battery storage, demand-side management and priority power supply for critical services during periods of extreme heat.

Low-cost interventions such as shaded bus stops, cooler pavements, tree-lined streets and improved pedestrian and cycling infrastructure could also reduce heat exposure, particularly in the Tarai and Kathmandu Valley, according to the report.

articles.title: Come together, right now
articles.summary:
On Thursday evening, Prime Minister Balendra Shah finally addressed the nation after days of unrest across the Tarai-Madhesh triggered by a communal clash in Dewanganj, Sunsari. Since recent events in regions of the southern plains placed the country in a precariously tense situation, it was only right that PM Shah finally took off his sunglasses and peered into the eyes of all citizens, urging them to exercise restraint and maintain societal harmony. The loss of three young lives—Jay Prakash Mehta, Om Prakash Mehta and Ganesh Yadav—and the injuries to scores of citizens and security personnel represent a dreadful tragedy that has heightened a sense of insecurity across the country. With curfews placed in several districts and the spectre of arson and vandalism looming, the fear persists that the situation could spiral beyond control, leading to irreparable damage to the national fabric.

PM Shah’s address to the nation on Thursday was a necessary intervention comprising an appeal for restraint and wisdom. The PM rightly asserted that religion is a “force that unites society and spreads love,” noting that “no religion or culture in the world teaches violence, hatred or division.” By emphasising that the fundamental essence of all religions is compassion, kindness, love and peace, he has sought to steer the public discourse away from the flames of retaliation scourging the Tarai-Madhesh. Such a message is vital in a society that has historically remained liberal towards diverse identities, viewing a mosaic of religions, castes and languages as a defining strength rather than a source of fracture.

Whilst the PM’s commitment to an impartial investigation and his consultation with President Ramchandra Paudel after the broadcast signal mature high-level engagement, the state must also acknowledge its earlier shortcomings. In the initial days of the unrest, security forces struggled with crowd management, and the government’s subsequent reliance on security-centric measures over political strategy was notable. The promotion of harmony now requires more than just the presence of law enforcement. It demands an inclusive strategy of social support and proactive political dialogue.

Furthermore, the inactivity of people’s representatives, particularly those from the Rastriya Swatantra Party who received a significant mandate in these regions, is a matter of concern. True leadership is defined by the ability to manage crises and provide reassurance directly to the electorate. There is an urgent need for representatives at all levels to visit their constituencies, fostering an atmosphere of trust rather than remaining silent in the face of communal tension.

The role of civil society, the media and social media users is equally indispensable. It is imperative to discourage provocative speech and the dissemination of false or unverified information that incites communal disharmony. Instead, the focus must shift towards the promotion of factual, restrained expression that celebrates co-existence.

Ultimately, the responsibility to ‘clear the clouds of unrest’ lies with both the state and the citizenry. Every individual must exercise the wisdom to analyse long-term consequences and reject the malicious interpretations of those seeking to destabilise the nation for ulterior motives. National unity has always been the greatest strength of Nepal during its most challenging periods.

The advancement of security and social harmony within the collective consciousness of a nation must remain the paramount objective of any responsible administration. However, the cultivation of such a climate cannot be achieved through the solitary efforts of the state. It necessitates a sustained, open dialogue and the unwavering support of every stakeholder within the national tapestry. In the words of the Beatles, the entire nation needs to ‘come together, right now’. The government must now act without further delay, prioritising open communication and ensuring that the preservation of social harmony remains the supreme duty of the state. Only through such a concerted effort can the nation transition from this period of unrest towards a future defined by peace and mutual respect.

articles.title: Is Nepal repeating India’s mistake?
articles.summary:
On Wednesday morning, in an interaction with a closed group of Nepali civil society members, Indian social activist Harsh Mander said that the ‘Citadel of fear’ in India’s socio-political landscape has been dismantled, but the ‘citadel of hate’ still stands. Mander was reflecting on the seismic impact of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in July. After Chief Justice of India Surya Kant labelled unemployed youth as ‘cockroaches’ on May 15, the CJP reclaimed the slur to forge a satirical, digitally organised group against the system. What began as an online campaign quickly transformed into a mass, leaderless uprising at New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, driven by fury over leaks in the NEET-UG medical entrance exams and a broader collapse of public trust.

The CJP movement was the inevitable explosion of friction points that have long simmered beneath the surface of the Indian state. For the middle and working class, standardised entrance exams are the primary vehicle for upward social mobility. When these papers leak, as they so often have over the years, years of family savings and student labour are erased. The system had normalised such leaks, with the perpetrators rarely receiving punishment. This was a breach of the meritocratic social contract.

While we regularly see opposition parties and their student wings, both politically motivated, protest paper leaks in India, the CJP protest marked a major departure from the nature of protests, somewhat mimicking September’s Gen Z protests in Nepal. Like Nepal’s movement, the ‘Instagram satyagrahis’ in India bypassed traditional, co-opted political student wings to build a ‘carnival of protest’ that used humour and meme warfare to strip the state of its ability to intimidate them. They forced the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and secured compensation for affected families.

While the current regime in Kathmandu rode to power on the popular anti-establishment rhetoric of September’s protest, Nepal still mirrors Mander’s analogy of citadels, albeit subtly, with a similar layer of digital toxicity that is quietly building a citadel of fear. Across social media platforms, there is an overwhelming, often blind support for the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) and the regime of Prime Minister Balendra Shah. RSP anti-establishment energy has curdled into an aggressive shield that suffocates democratic discourse. Anyone who dares to critique the government faces immediate, seemingly coordinated cyber-harassment.

This digital lynch-mob culture has become so intense that seasoned journalists and public intellectuals have started to self-censor their opinions. The new generation of civil society leaders have been forced to meet behind closed doors, as was the case in Mander’s interaction programme, similar to the underground meetings after Gyanendra’s coup d'état. A portion of these online enforcers can be traced to online groups like Men’s Room Reloaded (MRR)—a Facebook group founded by PM Shah’s chief adviser Kumar Byanjankar—that originated in toxic, pornographic subcultures. This, however, is not an avant-garde practice of the current regime. Previously, the CPN-UML erected an IT cell to cloud critiques against the party and its leaders with opinion-muzzling comments. That such groups are the digital enforcement arms for ruling parties has created a pervasive climate of fear. It was true of UML’s leadership, and it is true now: When citizens are afraid to speak, the vital feedback loops of a healthy democracy are severed.

While the digital citadel of fear rises in Kathmandu, a citadel of hate is simultaneously being constructed along the Tarai belt. The recent communal violence in Sunsari’s Dewanganj, which left one young man dead and 22 others injured, is a chilling warning for the Nepali state. Allegedly triggered by a dispute over loud music during a Bolbam procession, this was not an isolated event. The Armed Police Force (APF) had flagged this growing communal divide three years ago, warning that organised attempts were being made to foment religious and ethnic divisions. The report explicitly urged the government to learn from communal violence elsewhere in South Asia to resolve disputes before they escalated into widespread unrest. However, these warnings were ignored by the political leadership.

If the root causes of the Sunsari incident are not investigated with absolute transparency, Nepal risks normalising the same culture of mob-lynching and communal polarisation that has plagued India for over a decade. The high-handedness of the security response in Sunsari, where police reportedly fired indiscriminately, only deepens public anger.

Meanwhile, silence from PM Shah during this crisis does not help the cause. Except for a social media statement, the PM has been conspicuously absent from the necessary acts of statesmanship. He did not attend the all-party meeting held to address the Sunsari unrest. In a time of national tension, a PM should be the calming voice of the nation, perhaps through a televised address, rather than a distant figure operating through a digital screen.

Furthermore, PM Shah’s relationship with President Ramchandra Paudel has become virtually non-existent, with no substantive consultations taking place in four months. If he continues to govern in isolation, relying on security forces to contain violence rather than political dialogue to prevent it, Nepal will transform into a citadel of hate where the state’s only language is force.

This pattern of administrative arrogance extends to the education sector. The recent Tribhuvan University (TU) leak, where Master of Business Studies (MBS) question papers surfaced in a WhatsApp group of over 1,000 members just five minutes into the exam, is a direct echo of the Indian NEET scandal. While Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel has been praised by his supporters for the swift arrest of the teacher responsible, this is merely a cosmetic PR move if the structural flaws are not addressed. True accountability extends beyond just catching a single ‘Sulav Sir’ to a total restoration of meritocracy in systems like TU and Lok Sewa. As seen in India, when young citizens feel that honest routes to success are rigged, the meritocratic social contract is breached, and their frustration eventually spills onto the streets.

Nepal’s leadership must realise that an anti-establishment origin story does not grant permanent immunity. The same digital tools that built the current regime’s platform can just as easily turn against them if they absorb the ills of the old guard. Governance requires transparent delivery and the courage to engage with criticism rather than social media optics.

When I interviewed Nepali geopolitical analyst Chandra Dev Bhatta for this paper in the aftermath of Nepal’s Gen Z protest, he said that the events in Nepal must have made India restless. While many dismissed Bhatta’s claim as far-fetched, it turned out to be true to an extent. The Indian movement shows that when a government refuses to engage in honest dialogue and chooses intimidation, public anger evolves into an unstoppable, decentralised force. Now, conversely, the events in India have stirred restlessness into the new generation of civil society leaders in Nepal.

Nepal can choose proactive accountability today, or it can continue down a path of enforced silence and digital intimidation until the dam of public patience breaks. The state can either mend the land through trust and integrity now, or wait for the streets to demand a final, unforgiving reckoning.
